symptom: after the decode cache (ako/mxcli#2160), a script creating 600 pages still spent a fifth of its 110 s in Reader.readMprContents: every listing after every write read every unit file of its type again, through the persisted store (a SQLite query and a zstd decode per unit) or os.ReadFile
cause: two things. Reader.InvalidateCache, which every write calls, emptied the whole in-memory content cache, although a write changes one unit. And a script run held no CacheUnitReads scope at all - only check's passes and describe did - so execution never had the cache to begin with
file: modelsdk/mpr/reader_units.go (readMprContentsUnder, InvalidateCache, buildUnitCache), modelsdk/mpr/reader.go (cachedContent, rowHashes), mdl/executor/executor.go (ExecuteProgramReportingStop)
insight: The Unit table already holds each unit's ContentsHash and the writer already updates it, so an entry stored under the row hash it was read with retires itself when its unit is rewritten and survives every other write - the same content-keyed rule as the decode cache, with nothing new to keep in sync. What InvalidateCache drops instead is the hashes: between a write and the next buildUnitCache nothing is known to be current, so nothing is served or stored. buildUnitCache must cache its own reads under the hash it has just scanned (readMprContentsUnder), or the unit-type index's read and the listing's read are two. A second-order effect cost an hour: a run that ends inside a cache scope flushes what it read to the persisted unit store, so a test counting UnitFileReads for an 'uncached' control afterwards sees store hits instead and reads as if nothing were read - count UnitFileReads + UnitStoreHits when the question is 'not served from memory'. Measured on PedApp: 120 file reads per added page statement before, 1 after.
